keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Spacious, syncopated G Aeolian reggae-tango verses that explode into an urgent Bb major punk-rock chorus
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: G minor is the relative minor of Bb major

mainProgression.progression: i - v - bVI - v - iv - bVII7sus4 - Isus4
mainProgression.description: Masterclass in descending diatonic voice leading: the verse steps down the G natural minor scale one degree at a time before hanging on suspended F7sus4 and Gsus4 chords.

sectionProgressions.section: Intro & Verse ('Roxanne, you don't have to put on the red light')
sectionProgressions.progression: Gm - Dm/F - Ebmaj7 - Dm7 - Cm7 - F7sus4 - Gsus4
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: i - v6 - bVI - v7 - iv7 - bVII7sus4 - Isus4
sectionProgressions.description: Crisp, staccato reggae-skank upstrokes on beats 2 and 4 with immediate left-hand fret-hand muting
Suspended fourth voicings that refuse to resolve to a standard major or minor triad, heightening tension
Full-throttle, downstroked eighth-note punk-rock power chords in the relative major (Bb)

harmonicFunction: Gm (i) - Tense minor tonic struck cleanly on the reggae off-beats
Dm/F & Dm7 (v) - Minor fifth chord smoothing the descent from G down to Eb
Ebmaj7 (bVI) - Lush major seventh color chord adding jazz sophistication
Cm7 & F7sus4 (iv - bVII) - Subdominant to backdoor dominant preparation
Gsus4 (Isus4) - Unresolved suspended tonic that leaves the verse hanging in mid-air

techniques.name: Reggae Skank Mutings & Suspended Voicings
techniques.description: Executing razor-sharp staccato chord stabs on the off-beats by squeezing and immediately releasing left-hand finger pressure across movable barre and sus4 shapes

sequence: Rest on beat 1 (where Stewart Copeland's kick and Sting's bass hit) and strike the chord sharply on the off-beat
Release left-hand pressure immediately after striking the strings so the chord cuts off dry
Walk smoothly down the A-string barre shapes: Ebmaj7 (6th fret) → Dm7 (5th fret) → Cm7 (3rd fret)
Let the F7sus4 and Gsus4 chords ring out with shimmering modulation before exploding into the Bb - F - Gm chorus
tips: Left-hand pressure release is the secret to the Police reggae chop—do not rely only on palm muting
Target the top four strings (D, G, B, high E) during the verse stabs so you stay out of the bass guitar's way
Switch to aggressive, palm-muted eighth-note downstrokes when the chorus hits
details.progression: Gm - Dm - Ebmaj7 - Dm7 - Cm7 - F7sus4 - Gsus4

techniques.name: Relative Major Metric Modulation & Driving Downstroke Chords
techniques.description: Transitioning instantly from sparse, syncopated reggae-tango stabs in G minor to full-throttle, downstroked punk-rock power chords in the relative major of Bb

notes: Chorus power chords: Bb5 (6-8-8-X-X-X), F5 (1-3-3-X-X-X), G5 (3-5-5-X-X-X)
Right-hand attack: Heavy downward pick strokes locking with Stewart Copeland's ride and snare pulse
Dynamic expansion: Going from pristine Roland Jazz Chorus clean to overdriven tube punch
sequence: Anticipate the chorus explosion on beat 1 immediately following the Gsus4 suspension
Dig into continuous eighth-note downstrokes across the Bb - F - Gm changes
Mute unplayed strings with the flesh of your fretting index finger
Drop immediately back to sparse reggae offbeat stabs when the verse returns
tips: Keep the right-hand wrist loose during the heavy chorus strumming to avoid forearm cramping at 134 BPM
Use a bridge single-coil pickup for maximum snap on the reggae chops, boosted with subtle overdrive on the chorus
Lock directly with the bass drum for that authentic 1978 new-wave punch

sections.name: Verse 1 Descending Reggae Stabs ('Roxanne, you don't have to put on the red light')
sections.description: Andy Summers' descending minor-key chord stabs with tight fret-hand muting and suspended cadences.
notes: Keep the Gm, Dm7, Ebmaj7, and Cm7 stabs ultra-short and percussive
Immediate left-hand pressure release on each chord chop
Feel the wide acoustic space between guitar and bass

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Suspended 4th Cadence (F7sus4 & Gsus4 Tension)
sections.description: The harmonic tension swells as Summers holds shimmering suspended fourth chords that refuse to resolve before the chorus explodes.
notes: Allow the suspended chords to ring out across the measures
Engage subtle tape echo or chorus modulation
Crescendo pick attack into beat 1 of the chorus

sections.name: Chorus 1 Explosive Relative Major Rock ('Roxanne!')
sections.description: High-energy chorus shifting to the relative major (Bb - F - Gm) with relentless downstroke drive.
notes: Drive eighth-note downstrokes on Bb5 and F5
Dig in with the pick to create stark dynamic contrast
Lock tightly with Copeland's kick drum

sections.name: Verse 2 Subtle Voicing Variations & Police Reggae Groove
sections.description: Second verse introducing delicate high-register triad voicings and echo trails weaving through Sting's vocal delivery.
notes: Focus on clear note separation across strings 2, 3, and 4
Listen to the chromatic inner voice descent: D → Eb → D → C
Keep the staccato offbeat chops razor-clean

sections.name: Chorus 2 Dynamic Punk-Rock Drive
sections.description: Second chorus with enhanced band velocity, backing vocal shouts, and full power-chord saturation.
notes: Full wall-of-sound power chords
Accent the snare hits on beats 2 and 4
Sing lead or backing vocal while maintaining downstroke rhythm

sections.name: Outro Extended Vocal Vamp & Rhythmic Fade
sections.technique: Continuous Power Chord Strumming & Fade Nuance
sections.description: The celebratory outro where the driving Bb - F - Gm chorus progression cycles under Sting's ecstatic vocal cries all the way to the fade.
notes: Maintain unwavering 134 BPM tempo
Subtle pick rake embellishments on chord transitions
Gradual decrescendo into the studio fadeout

guitar.recommended: Modified 1961 Fender Telecaster Custom (with neck PAF humbucker and phase switch)
guitar.pickup: Bridge single-coil for biting reggae stabs; middle/both pickups for chorus fullness

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 1959 100W or Roland JC-120 Jazz Chorus

effects.distortion: MXR Distortion+ or Marshall preamp overdrive for the chorus
effects.delay: Maestro Echoplex EP-3 tape delay (short slapback echo)
effects.other: Electro-Harmonix Electric Mistress Flanger / Boss CE-2W Chorus for shimmering modulation

beginner.title: Chord Shapes & Chorus Power Chords
steps: Learn the movable minor 7th and major 7th barre shapes: Gm, Ebmaj7, Dm7, and Cm7
Practice the chorus power chords (Bb5 - F5 - G5) with steady eighth-note downstrokes
Play through the verse chord sequence in simple whole notes to memorize the order

intermediate.title: Staccato Reggae Chop & Sus4 Chords
steps: Master the fret-hand squeeze-and-release muting technique on the verse stabs
Voice the F7sus4 and Gsus4 chords cleanly at the end of each verse cycle
Lock into the 134 BPM off-beat groove without rushing

advanced.title: Full Dynamic Control & Summers Modulation
steps: Transition instantaneously from razor-thin staccato verse stabs to roaring punk-rock choruses
Add authentic Andy Summers upper-voicing variations and tape-echo rhythmic trails
Maintain pocket precision during the extended vocal-improv outro

commonMistakes: Holding the verse chord shapes down continuously instead of releasing left-hand pressure immediately
Dragging the tempo during the transition into the high-energy chorus
Overplaying on the low strings during the verse, muddying Sting's bassline
practiceRoutine: 10 minutes: Fret-hand squeeze-and-release muting drill on a single Gm chord at 100-134 BPM
15 minutes: Descending verse chord progression (Gm - Dm7 - Ebmaj7 - Dm7 - Cm7 - F7sus4 - Gsus4)
15 minutes: Sudden dynamic shift from verse reggae chops into full eighth-note chorus power chords
focusAreas: Dynamic contrast between clean reggae verses and overdriven rock choruses
metronomeWork: Set metronome to 134 BPM and practice landing the verse chord chops strictly on the '&' of each beat
